nodes.title: Graphiti Fractal — FM-13 Search-Path Diagnosis
nodes.summary: Completed instrumentation experiment localizing where broad retrieval noise enters the measured path: BM25 generated broad candidates, RRF preserved them, and the constructed CrossEncoder was not invoked.
nodes.why_read: Open when reconstructing why the research did not immediately replace models: FM-13 first proved that the measured path did not call the CrossEncoder and that broad candidate generation was not the same as final qualification failure.

research.research_question: Where does measured retrieval noise first enter, and which ranking components are actually invoked?
research.origin_problem: The Zephyr no-answer query returned unrelated stored facts, but the active search path had not yet been instrumented.
prior_evidence: Persistence and retrieval plumbing had bounded positive evidence before relevance became the bottleneck.
competing_hypotheses: CrossEncoder may be failing to reject noise.
Broad candidate generation plus fusion may be operating without a qualification gate.
results: MemoryOps was pass-through for the measured edge ordering/facts
Zephyr returned all four stored facts despite empty relevance gold
limitations: Broad candidate generation itself is not automatically a defect
rejected_interpretations: The tested CrossEncoder failed; it was not invoked.
BM25 broadness alone proves BM25 is broken.
open_questions: Would real semantic embeddings improve the candidate geometry enough to solve final relevance filtering?

nodes.title: Graphiti Fractal — FM-14 Real Embedding Differential
nodes.summary: Completed one-variable experiment replacing deterministic embeddings with local BGE semantic embeddings. Geometry improved, but final hybrid filtering remained insufficient and the Zephyr no-answer query still returned four unrelated facts.
nodes.why_read: Open to see why real embeddings weakened the 'fake geometry caused everything' hypothesis without solving absolute candidate rejection.

research.research_question: Are real semantic embeddings alone sufficient to remove the observed relevance failure?
research.origin_problem: FM-13 showed the active path used deterministic embedding geometry and did not invoke the CrossEncoder.
prior_evidence: FM-13 localized broad candidates and zero CrossEncoder calls.
competing_hypotheses: Deterministic hash-space embeddings may be the main cause.
Even real semantic geometry may still require a separate qualification stage.
results: Real BGE geometry improved top ordering.
Q1–Q3 macro Precision@1, Recall@3 and MRR were 1.0 on the tiny fixture.
Q4 Zephyr still returned four unrelated facts.
limitations: The full pairwise cosine matrix happened to be separable; active search/fusion/filtering remained the failure surface.
open_questions: Does a stronger pairwise query↔fact scorer expose useful direct-answer discrimination?

nodes.title: Graphiti Fractal — FM-15 Real CrossEncoder Pairwise Signal
nodes.summary: Completed direct pairwise scoring experiment using local BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 on the frozen 20 query↔fact pairs. Useful CE discrimination was confirmed on the tiny fixture; no global threshold, runtime gate, or general superiority claim was established.
nodes.why_read: Open for the exact small-fixture pairwise CE evidence and the Q5 component boundary that later forced direct-answer relevance to be separated from multi-hop answer-support components.
nodes.notes: The raw artifact records cross_encoder_signal_effect=STRONGLY_IMPROVED. Later review narrowed the safe claim: pairwise CE signal is confirmed on this fixture, while NEW_SEPARABILITY_VS_EMBEDDINGS is not established because FM-14 embeddings were also separable on the tiny matrix and the score scales differ.

research.research_question: Does a real local CrossEncoder provide useful pairwise query↔fact relevance signal on the frozen fixture?
research.origin_problem: FM-14 improved geometry but did not provide honest rejection in the active hybrid path.
prior_evidence: FM-14 real embeddings improved top ordering but Zephyr still returned false positives.
competing_hypotheses: A pairwise CrossEncoder may contain stronger direct-answer discrimination.
Any apparent gap may be only tiny-fixture luck and may not generalize.
results: Q5 direct support = false; co-retrieval observed; multi-hop reasoning not proven
limitations: FM-14 embeddings also had fixture-specific separability
CE sigmoid and cosine scores are not directly comparable scales
rejected_interpretations: CrossEncoder is universally better than embeddings.
open_questions: Can the pairwise signal generalize to held-out entities, hard negatives, broad queries and no-answer cases?

nodes.title: Graphiti Fractal — FM-16 Held-Out Ranking & Global-Threshold Feasibility
nodes.summary: Completed frozen CAL/TEST experiment comparing BGE CrossEncoder and embedding score families under mixed-query constraints. CE ranked better, but neither family had one feasible global raw threshold; strict later H1 fails for both and Honest Empty was not established.
nodes.why_read: Open for the raw frozen run_007 outcome; then open the closure document for the reconciled interpretation because the raw result contains broad comparator labels later narrowed by independent review.
nodes.notes: Raw result.json contains ce_vs_embedding=NO_MATERIAL_GAIN. Reconciled closure narrows this to global-threshold qualification only: CE_VS_EMBEDDING_RANKING=CE_BETTER; CE_VS_EMBEDDING_GLOBAL_QUALIFICATION=NO_MATERIAL_ADVANTAGE; overall=MIXED.

research.research_question: Does pairwise relevance signal generalize under held-out mixed-query evaluation, and can one CAL-derived global threshold support answer recall plus no-answer empty behavior?
research.origin_problem: FM-15 confirmed pairwise CE signal only on a tiny fixture and did not test held-out global qualification.
prior_evidence: FM-15 pairwise CE signal on run_006
Independent protocol review forced direct-answer, component and related-context separation before execution.
competing_hypotheses: CE may rank better and support one global threshold.
CE may rank better but absolute score regimes may overlap across query classes.
Embeddings may be similarly sufficient under the same threshold contract.
limitations: Chronology/leakage barrier plausible but not independently cryptographically provable
rejected_interpretations: theta=null means no relevant memory exists.
Global threshold infeasible means CrossEncoder is useless.
FM-16 selects structure, LLM recognition, graph/path scoring or another next architecture.
open_questions: What minimal observable mechanism removes the residual qualification error class?

nodes.title: Retrieval Relevance Track — pre-FM-16 execution snapshot
nodes.summary: Historical 2026-09-10 research-track snapshot that accurately explains FM-13–FM-15 and protocol hardening but predates run_007 and therefore has stale current-frontier text about FM-16 not yet being executed.
nodes.why_read: Open for the pre-execution narrative and protocol-review history, but never use its 'FM-16 not run' frontier text as current state. Reopen the FM-16 closure and FM-17-pre STOP boundary for currentness.

nodes.title: Zephyr no-answer negative control
nodes.summary: Recurring frozen negative-control pattern: a query about Project Zephyr has no relevant stored answer while retrieval still produces related/best-available candidates, exposing ranking-without-qualification behavior.
nodes.why_read: Use this concept to understand the original failure mode: returning the best available candidate is not the same as returning an acceptable answer, and no relevant stored result does not prove world-level absence.

nodes.title: Honest Empty / NO_RELEVANT_MEMORY research target
nodes.summary: Research target requiring a system to distinguish candidates-exist-but-none-answer from zero candidates, filtering, failure, timeout, and ambiguous query states without forced refill or world-level absence claims.
nodes.why_read: Open whenever 'empty' is discussed. The concept is a target and status distinction, not a solved runtime mechanism; FM-16 explicitly did not establish it.

nodes.title: Direct Answer ≠ Multi-Hop Component ≠ Related Context ≠ Nonanswer
nodes.summary: Task-definition distinction developed during FM-15→FM-16 review and protected in FM-17-pre so required answer-support components are not treated as direct answers or accidentally filtered as generic non-gold noise.
nodes.why_read: Use when constructing or interpreting relevance gold, hard negatives, broad queries, or multi-hop retrieval. It prevents direct-answer precision from being optimized by deleting necessary components.
